prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full round-1 exchange I keep a single-part prize on B019 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The scientific chain from proglucagon processing and incretin physiology, through identification of the bioactive GLP-1(7-36/37) peptide and receptor biology, to agonists with benefits in glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes, is complete, independently confirmed in large randomised trials and mature. No other shortlisted achievement matches it on both mechanism and measured effect on patients. Round 1 showed unanimity on the configuration, but I do not lean on that count. I re-examined the case for the three names on the merits and the reasons I gave still hold. A single part also avoids cutting B019 below three names to make room for a second achievement that no member has put in a preferred configuration.
statement.case_against: The attribution question has not been resolved by round 1. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide against Habener's group cannot be settled from the supplied record, and several of us said so. Knudsen is outside the three-person cap, and a discovery-centred prize does not name the half-life engineering that turned a hormone into a once-weekly drug. The citation can acknowledge that step in its wording about therapies made possible, but it cannot give her credit. If the committee finds that the record does not support Mojsov, the prize should become a Holst and Drucker pair or give the third place to Knudsen. I would then favour the pair, because replacing a discovery with a development contribution changes what the prize is for.

responses.point: Knudsen's liraglutide and semaglutide design is arguably as decisive for patients as the physiology, and the choice between Mojsov and Knudsen is a matter of judgement about industrial development.
responses.response: This is the strongest challenge to my configuration and I took it seriously. I agree that the drugs would not exist as medicines without half-life engineering. My conclusion is different. The prize rewards a discovery that changed a field, and the active peptide and the physiology it revealed are what made the engineering a rational project. The acylated analogues are a development of that discovery. I would not remove Mojsov for Knudsen unless the record showed her priority to be unsupported. In that case I would still name Holst and Drucker, rather than replacing a discoverer with a drug designer. I have not changed this from round 1, but my confidence is lower than it was and I would say so openly.

responses.point: A single-achievement prize is cleanest because the three GLP-1 names fill the cap and a second part would only force someone out.
responses.response: I agree and now hold this more firmly than in round 1. If B012 or B030 were added, the GLP-1 allocation would drop to one or two names, and the person excluded would be one of the physiologists whose work is the basis of the whole chain. B012 would also still have its own six-name problem. I do not see a second part that is worth that cost. I remain with you on Linnarsson's view that Knudsen would be the first replacement only if Mojsov's claim failed. Where I differ is that I would not treat that replacement as automatic. The pair is also a coherent prize.

responses.point: B040 (Walter and Mori) is a conceptually original candidate with a clean pair of names, and a mechanism-led discovery could compete with therapy-linked candidates.
responses.response: I accept that the UPR is a real conceptual advance, confirmed over decades, and Walter and Mori are the natural names. My reservation is the same as in round 1. Ron's and Kaufman's work on PERK and ATF6 means the pair is less clean than it looks, and the human disease link is mostly mechanistic and without a therapy. As a second part it would still reduce B019, so it fails for the same reason as B012 and B030. I did not change my view, but it is a candidate for a later year, not a poor one.

responses.point: Mojsov's priority is contested, and if the committee wanted to honour translation, the discovery trio would be the wrong one.
responses.response: I agree with the conditional. If the committee decides that translation should be recognised, the trio changes. I do not think that is the right reading here, because the discovery side already stands on a very strong clinical result, which the citation can state. I would also resist treating uncertainty about Mojsov as proof against her. We lack the historical record, and a committee that cannot verify a priority claim should check it with documents before voting, not drop her on recollection. If it cannot be resolved, Holst and Drucker are the secure core.

responses.point: The evidence supplied is not sufficient to drop the discovery trio, and a split with B030 would shrink the GLP-1 allocation below three names.
responses.response: I agree. The chair's questions asked whether to split, and I answer no. B030 has strong haematological proof, but the attribution is open (Eshhar, and whether the achievement is CAR engineering or cell therapy more broadly), and late toxicities and limited solid-tumour effect remain unsettled. B030 does not outweigh the cost of leaving out a GLP-1 discoverer. On B012, which is in my own field, I should be explicit that I do not think its being in my field is a reason to favour it. The six names do not fit three places, and Bamberg, Boyden or Miesenboeck would be left out of any trio.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against Habener's group can be supported by the documentary record, which none of us can check from the supplied files.
Whether the committee will treat Knudsen's medicinal chemistry as part of the discovery or as a separate development, and how the citation should acknowledge it without naming her.
Whether a fair three-person group exists for B012, or whether it should wait until the credit question is clearer.
How much weight long-term safety, including effects in pregnancy and in young patients, should carry as evidence accumulates.
statement.conflict_note: Unchanged from round 1. My profile records a 2019 Physiol Rev co-authorship with Sten Grillner, joint work with Patrik Ernfors, and a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons. None involves a shortlisted credited name, so I see no recusal need. B012 concerns circuit neuroscience, my own field, but I have no documented tie to its credited names and I treat it as an alternative only. No other member has disclosed a tie to me that changes this.
